clue.text: Delicate creature in musical requiring nude performance

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical famous for its nude scene
to streak is to run naked in public, so a streak is a nude performance

explanation.surface: A fragile performer in a stage show is required to appear naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delicate creature' sounds like a shy actor; it is a butterfly. 'in' and 'requiring' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The hairstreak is a small, fragile butterfly, a delicate winged insect.

clue.text: Return as it happens, pernicious

indicators.note: Return tells us to send the following word back the way it came, reading it backwards

parts.note: a broadcast shown as it happens is live

explanation.surface: Coming back exactly as events unfold is somehow harmful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernicious means harmful and wicked in effect, a close synonym of wicked or malign.

clue.text: In retreat, testament hard for Holy Roman Emperor

indicators.note: In places the testament and hard pieces inside the word for a retreat

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den, a place of retreat
OT is short for the Old Testament
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: While withdrawn, a will was hard on a medieval emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothair I was a Carolingian ruler who held the title of Holy Roman Emperor in the ninth century.

clue.text: For example, a hundred and nine dinosaurs

definitions.text: For example, a hundred and nine
definitions.meaning: 100 is ten times ten and 9 is three times three
dinosaurs here are old-fashioned, conventional people

explanation.surface: Some numbers are offered as examples alongside prehistoric reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers made by multiplying a whole number by itself are squares; fuddy-duddies are also called squares.

clue.text: Measure of weight written with atomic number of hydrogen gas

parts.note: OZ is the abbreviation for ounce, a unit of weight
hydrogen is element number one in the periodic table

explanation.surface: A weight unit is noted alongside hydrogen's place in the periodic table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written with' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, a gas in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Observe cloth the wrong way round on brown overalls

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the preceding pieces after the colour word that follows

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: the wrong way round says both observe and cloth pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: to observe is to see
a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone notices fabric back to front on brown work clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' turns SEE+RAG into GAREES, which sits on DUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are trousers with a bib and straps, a kind of overalls worn for manual work.

clue.text: A little artistic talent in couture, a sellout on tour

indicators.note: on tour suggests the letters travelling about and ending up in a new order

explanation.surface: Fashion house shows sell out while travelling the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The definition is a joke: the painter was famously very short, so a little artistic talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, a French painter, stood under five feet tall, a small man of great artistic gifts.

clue.text: A smashing song for children?

parts.note: a nursery counting song in which glass containers hanging on a wall fall off one by one, and so presumably smash

explanation.surface: A really great nursery song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' looks like praise, meaning excellent; in fact the bottles in the song fall and break.
explanation.definitionFit: This children's counting song has bottles falling off a wall in turn, which would literally be smashing.

clue.text: Scottish island with peculiar trait, as characteristic

indicators.note: peculiar, meaning odd, signals the letters of trait set in a strange order

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde, western Scotland

explanation.surface: An island off Scotland is known for an odd feature as its defining quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' turns TRAIT into ATTRI; 'with' and 'as' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic is a distinguishing quality or feature, which is what an attribute is.

clue.text: Opener for Gloucestershire caught by spin, getting top edge

indicators.note: caught by places the opening letter inside the word for a spin, held within it

parts.note: a spin is a short ride, as in a spin in the car

indicators.note: Opener for takes just the opening letter of the county name

explanation.surface: A Gloucestershire opening batsman, caught off a spinner, gets an edge at the top of his bat.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (opener, caught, spin, edge) is all misdirection. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the long narrow top edge of a roof or mountain.

clue.text: Figure leader of Conservatives back in office

indicators.note: in places the leader and back pieces inside the word for an office

parts.note: a den is a private room for work, a study or office

indicators.note: leader of takes just the opening letter of Conservatives

parts.note: back, as in 'years back', means ago

explanation.surface: A Tory leader returns to his job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a party leader back in office; in fact C and AGO go into DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a plane shape with ten sides, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Ornamental style is dismissed by toff — that's taken about a month

indicators.note: taken about means the trimmed toff word is wrapped around the month
dismissed by says the word is goes out of the toff word

parts.note: a toff is an upper-class person, informally an aristo
DEC is short for December

explanation.surface: An upper-class twit throws someone out, and a month passes.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking IS from ARISTO leaves ARTO, which goes around DEC; 'that's' is a link. A toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is the geometric decorative style in design and architecture of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Fish tails from dinner you discard, horrid

indicators.note: tails from takes the final letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Someone throws away the scraps of fish left from a horrible meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a freshwater fish of the carp family found in European rivers and lakes.

clue.text: A shade down alongside ring and two crosses?

indicators.note: alongside puts the down word next to the other pieces, here following them

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
X is the shape of a cross
a ford is a place where a river is crossed
feeling down is feeling blue

explanation.surface: A colour is sad, next to a circle and a couple of X marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two crosses' gives two different pieces: X (a cross shape) and FORD (a river crossing).
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford blue is a dark navy shade, the colour of Oxford University's sports teams.

clue.text: Solar reflector's warmth containing rising Earth temperature

indicators.note: containing says the warmth word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: warmth is heat

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading the word upward, so backwards

parts.note: earth in the sense of ground is soil

explanation.surface: A sun mirror gives out heat while the planet's temperature goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SOIL into LIOS. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliostat is a mirror turned by clockwork to keep reflecting sunlight onto a fixed point.

clue.text: First notes in report nicely written up

indicators.note: written up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Opening remarks in a report are written up nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tells you to look inside 'report nicely'; 'written up' means read upwards, so backwards, in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece of music, its first notes.

clue.text: Swimmer with type of school sport

parts.note: a skate is a flat fish, so a swimmer
a boarding school is one where pupils live in term time

explanation.surface: A swimmer goes to a particular kind of school for games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person; it is the fish. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Skateboarding is riding a wheeled board, a recreational and competitive sport.

clue.text: Church screen rose when moved to obscure cardinal

indicators.note: to obscure says the rearranged flower word covers and so contains the cardinal word
when moved says the letters of rose are shifted into another order

parts.note: cardinal is a deep scarlet colour, red

explanation.surface: A rose got up and moved to hide a senior churchman behind a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when moved' makes ROSE into RE..OS, around RED. 'cardinal' looks like the churchman; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or panel behind the altar of a church.

clue.text: Eleven arms?

definitions.meaning: a football team of eleven players, here the London club
a store of weapons; the question mark flags the second reading

explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, and a team fields eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is both a famous English football team, an eleven, and a stockpile of weapons.

clue.text: In a particular column, alter verb that's irregular

indicators.note: irregular, as with grammar's irregular verbs, signals the letters set out of order

explanation.surface: Change a verb that doesn't follow the usual grammatical pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' is the spinal column, not a newspaper column.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertebral means relating to the spine, the backbone or spinal column.

clue.text: Saving time, female keeps fresh

indicators.note: Saving here means the female word keeps the time letter safe inside it

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: To save time, a woman keeps food fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that lasts stays fresh and usable, continuing in good condition.

clue.text: Pure ecstasy smuggled in without a hard-core classification?

indicators.note: smuggled in says the drug letter is slipped secretly inside the other piece

parts.note: a film not rated for adults only could be called un-adult-rated
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Neat ecstasy is smuggled in without a hardcore label.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful 'classification' reads as a film certificate: UN (not) ADULT RATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadulterated means unmixed and free from added substances, completely pure.

clue.text: Engineer continued behind the scenes?

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, signalling the letters reorganised

explanation.surface: An engineer kept working out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a person, but it is a verb meaning rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done behind the scenes happens out of sight, so escapes attention.

clue.text: Start on caviar, while queen tucks into fish dish

indicators.note: Start on takes the opening letter of caviar

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'

indicators.note: tucks into places the queen piece inside the fish word

parts.note: sole is a flatfish
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: After beginning on caviar, the Queen tucks into a fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' sounds like eating, but it puts ER in SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a slow-cooked stew, also the dish it is cooked in.

clue.text: Queen in love embraced by old date in March?

indicators.note: embraced by places the three pieces inside the word for old

parts.note: ex means former, so old
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A queen in love is hugged by a former partner on a spring date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a piece (IN), not a link. The question mark admits the date is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring equinox, when day and night are equal, falls around 20 March.

clue.text: Following worker, perhaps, upset Scandinavian king is cross

indicators.note: Following puts the king piece after the worker piece

parts.note: a worker bee is one kind of bee

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, so reads it backwards

parts.note: Olaf is a name borne by several kings of Norway

explanation.surface: After a labourer, an upset Nordic monarch gets angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns OLAF into FALO. 'cross' looks like 'angry'; it means a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefalo is a hybrid of domestic cattle and American bison, a cross-breed.

clue.text: Poisoner has run, heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the word for run loses its first letter

parts.note: a run in tights is a ladder, in British usage

explanation.surface: A poisoner has fled, getting away.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a ladder is a run in stockings. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is a venomous snake, Britain's only poisonous one, so a poisoner.

clue.text: Live in the lap of luxury under leadership of dictator

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the luxury word below the dictator letter
leadership of takes just the leading letter of dictator

parts.note: to live in the lap of luxury is to live well

explanation.surface: Under a dictator's rule, some live in great luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or make one's home somewhere.
